statement: Generating candidate record-to-skeleton mappings from shared cluster membership and then reading each substrate rejected 378 of 419 candidates (90.2 percent), and the typical rejection is not a weak relationship but an absent quantity — one skeleton needs coupling weights w_ij while the candidate island states as its own barrier that the connectome arrives with weights stripped. Two cautions travel with this number: the further 7 drops among the 41 accepted were skeleton-attribution conflicts and judge self-flags, so folding them in to reach 91.9 percent would mix two failure modes; and this does not contradict the upstream pre-registered reconciliation of 65.4 percent against a 12.8 percent weighted-random baseline, which asks which domains a skeleton appears in rather than which record instantiates it.

statement: The live record table (1848) and the retirement ledger (18) partition the issued id space exactly: they sum to 1866, which is max(n), with zero overlap and zero ids that are in neither. The retirement ledger therefore accounts for every id ever issued, a completeness property the publisher bookkeeping cannot produce on its own because it knows what it recorded and not what it missed. Two limits, both stated by the upstream and accepted here: reproducing this reads the same two source files, so agreement on the arithmetic is not independent verification of the sources; and the check cannot detect a lost retirement entry whose id was reassigned to a new record, since that leaves no hole either — it rules out omission, not rewriting.
evidence: audit/atlas_data.json records[].n and audit/retired-domain-directions.json retired[].n
upstream reproduced independently and logged both limits in its own ledger

statement: Structure mappings in this repository carry no provenance field at all — it is undefined for all 135 mappings at runtime, so every one of the 61 corpus record ids pinned by the structure plane comes from structure-level provenance. Mappings ground themselves the other way, through evidenceRefs holding resolvable URLs, which 85 of 135 carry. Anyone extracting record ids from this repository should not look in the mapping layer: the ids are not merely hard to find there, they are absent.

statement: None of the ten corpus files that express relations relates one record to another: scanning every integer field in the issued id range across all of them returns zero references, and the relations they do carry run question-to-question by string id and entity-to-cluster by cluster code. This corroborates the separately established fact that all 136 isomorphism domain slots have a null record id. The consequence for a consumer is that a relational layer over records cannot be projected from this corpus and has to be authored downstream — and that generating it from shared cluster membership is the weak proxy already recorded here, so the absence cannot be filled by inference either.

statement: Mechanical quantity-level matching does not generate reviewable structure-mapping candidates either, measured twice on the 222 islands that sit in no authored relational layer. Matching CJK bigrams from a structure authored quantities against an island own depth text produced 4393 candidates reaching 222 of 222 islands, and a matcher that reaches every island discriminates nothing; the surviving pairs were joined by boundary-spanning fragments. Restricting to rare technical English terms cut it to 1936 candidates but still reached 222 of 222 at one term and leaked function words such as already and rather into the two-term set. This extends the recorded finding that cluster adjacency is a weak proxy: the failure is in candidate generation and it is not fixed by changing which surface feature is matched. What did work was reading the substrate, and the strongest single signal is the island own barrier field, which in several cases states the structure required quantity as missing or present in the structure own vocabulary.

probe v2 (rare English terms, df<=2): 1995 raw, 59 barrier-vetoed, 1936 kept, 222/222 at >=1 term, 365 at >=2 over 170 islands
